intro: A ranked canon — films that did permanent damage, in the good sense. The Letterboxd diary below updates on its own.
note: Ordering below the top two is provisional; edit freely.

films.title: Strange Circus
films.note: Guignol memory-theatre — abuse, authorship, and a cello. Nothing else is built like it.

films.title: Perfect Blue
films.note: Identity dissolving across screens before the internet had finished arriving.

films.title: Cure
films.note: Hypnosis as contagion; the emptiest interiors in cinema.

films.title: Pulse
films.note: Loneliness made literal haunting. The dial-up dread has only aged truer.

films.title: The House That Jack Built
films.note: Art-as-atrocity confession, with Virgil along for the descent.

films.title: No Country for Old Men
films.note: Fate carries a captive-bolt pistol; the ending refuses every catharsis.

films.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
films.note: Maximalist multiverse collapsing into a mother and a daughter.

films.title: Koyaanisqatsi
films.note: Civilization at time-lapse speed until Glass turns it into liturgy.

films.title: Paprika
films.note: The dream-machine film everything after it borrowed from.

films.title: Shortbus
films.note: Post-9/11 New York looking for connection with the lights on.

films.title: Lost Highway
films.note: The psychogenic fugue as Möbius strip.

films.title: Zima Blue
films.note: Sixteen minutes on art, memory, and the return to the tile.
